events.title: Hernando de Soto Claims Florida for Spain
events.description: Spanish conquistador Hernando de Soto landed on the Florida coast and claimed the territory for the Spanish crown. His expedition went on to push deep into the American Southeast.
events.significance: The expedition was among the first European journeys into the interior of what is now the United States. It brought the first sustained contact between Europeans and many Indigenous nations of the region.

events.title: "Casey at the Bat" Is Published
events.description: Ernest Lawrence Thayer's comic poem about a mighty slugger's famous strikeout appeared in the San Francisco Examiner.
events.significance: The poem became one of the best-loved works in American popular culture. It helped cement baseball's place in the national imagination.

events.title: Franz Kafka Dies
events.description: The Prague-born writer died at age 40 of tuberculosis, having published only a small share of his work in his lifetime.
events.significance: Kafka's posthumously published novels, including The Trial and The Castle, made him one of the most influential authors of the 20th century. The word "Kafkaesque" is now used for nightmarish bureaucracy.

events.title: Pope John XXIII Dies
events.description: The beloved pontiff, known as "the good pope," died in Vatican City after a short papacy. He had convened the Second Vatican Council in 1962.
events.significance: The council he opened reshaped the Catholic Church, modernizing its liturgy and opening it to dialogue with other faiths.

events.title: Gemini 4 Launches
events.description: NASA launched Gemini 4 with astronauts James McDivitt and Ed White on the first multi-day American space mission. During the flight, White became the first American to walk in space.
events.significance: The mission showed that astronauts could work outside a spacecraft and endure longer flights. Both were key steps toward the Apollo Moon landings.
